topics.title: Loci
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: Describe common types of loci. (k, u)
Construct loci involving points under given conditions. (u, s)
Construct loci involving inequalities. (u, s, v/a)

body.text: A locus (plural loci) is the set of all points that satisfy a given condition. The locus of points a fixed distance from a point is a circle; the locus of points equidistant from two fixed points is the perpendicular bisector of the line joining them; the locus of points equidistant from two lines is the angle bisector between them.

A goat is tethered by a 3 m rope to the corner of a rectangular building. The locus of points the goat can reach is three-quarters of a circle of radius 3 m around that corner (the building blocks the rest), unless the rope is long enough to wrap around an adjacent corner, in which case a smaller circular arc extends around that second corner too.

Where two loci must both be true at once (e.g. "equidistant from points A and B" AND "5 cm from point C"), the solution is the intersection of the two individual loci — draw both (a perpendicular bisector and a circle) and mark where they cross.

A locus involving an inequality, such as "less than 4 cm from point P", is a region rather than a line — in this case, the inside of a circle of radius 4 cm centred at P, usually shown shaded with a dashed boundary since the boundary itself (exactly 4 cm) is excluded.
